monsters.name: Awakened One

moves.name: Sludge
effects: Adds a Void into your draw pile.

monsters.ai:
Phase One
Always starts with Slash.
Every turn after:
* Soul Strike 25% chance
* Slash 75% chance
Slash cannot be used three times in a row. Soul Strike cannot be used twice in a row.
Phase Two
Once its HP reaches 0, it loses Curiosity and its intent changes to Rebirth. Any Strength gained from Curiosity is kept.
Always starts Phase Two with Dark Echo. Afterward, it has a 50/50 chance to use Tackle or Sludge. It cannot use either of these moves three times in a row.
The remaining Cultists will flee when the Awakened One is defeated in Phase Two.

monsters.name: Bronze Orb

moves.name: Stasis
effects: Steals a random card of the highest rarity from your draw pile (or discard pile, if the draw pile is empty).
On death, returns the card to your hand.

monsters.ai:
Each Bronze Orb can only use Stasis once per combat. Stasis has a 75% chance to be used each turn until it has been picked. After using Stasis Bronze Orb has a 70% chance to use Support Beam and a 30% chance to use Beam each turn. Bronze Orb cannot use the same attack thrice in a row.
Stasis
Stasis will always prioritize the highest rarity Card in your draw pile. If your draw pile is empty, Stasis will pick from your discard pile instead. Cards in Stasis will not be affected by certain variables; for example, Masterful Stab's Energy cost will not increase even if the player takes damage.

monsters.name: Hexaghost

moves.name: Divider
effects: N = Player's HP at the start of the turn, divided by 12 (rounded down).

moves.name: Sear
effects: Adds 1 (A19: 2) Burns into your discard pile.

moves.name: Inferno
effects: Adds 3 Burns+ into your discard pile.
For the rest of combat, any Burn created by Sear will be upgraded.

monsters.ai:
Always starts with Activate followed by Divider.
For the rest of combat, repeats the following pattern:
# Sear
# Tackle
# Sear
# Inflame
# Tackle
# Sear
# Inferno
monsters.notes:
* This fight is a race to kill Hexaghost before turn 9. Before that, Hexaghost isn't very threatening, prefering to fire low damage Sears and Tackles. However, on the 9th turn, it will use Inferno, which deals 24 (30 (A4), 36 (A19)) damage and fills your discard pile with Burns+. It's very hard to survive this attack, let alone the turns after.
** To kill Hexaghost in 9 turns, on average you need to deal around 30 damage per turn. Achieving this requires some sort of scaling, such as Strength or Poison.
* On the 2nd turn, Hexaghost uses Divider, the only attack in the game that scales with your current HP. If you are already low on health, this attack deals pitiful damage. Therefore, it's often preferable to not rest before this fight, and instead upgrade a card that will help you beat Hexaghost before Inferno.
** For example, if you have between 12 and 23 HP, Divider deals only 12 damage, easily blocked.

* During the Elite encounter, you should focus in eliminating the 1st or the 3rd Sentry as fast as possible, ignoring the 2nd one. This prevents you from taking 18 (20 (A3)) damage each other turn, making the rest of the fight much easier.

monsters.name: Slime Boss

moves.name: Goop Spray
effects: Adds 3 (A19: 5) Slimed into your discard pile.

moves.name: Split
effects: Disappears and spawns 1 Acid Slime (L) and 1 Spike Slime (L) with its current HP.

monsters.ai:
Repeats the following pattern:
#Goop Spray
#Preparing
#Slam
Once its HP reaches 50% or lower, its current Intent will be immediately changed to Split.
monsters.notes:
* Until Slime Boss splits, Slam is the only way it can harm you. Other than this attack, it spends most of the fight doing nothing. There are many ways to deal with it other than with Block and Weak:
** As long as you can deal 70 (75 (A9)) damage by turn 3, you can force Slime Boss to split before it attacks.
** You may fully negate Slam with Buffer, Fossilized Helix, Incense Burner and Ghost in a Jar.
** Rest before the fight to have more than 35 (38 (A4)) HP, then simply tank it. After all, you always heal after boss fights.
* Split creates two Large Slimes with Slime Boss' remaining HP. Thus it's better to cause Slime Boss to lose as much health as possible before the splitting.
** This can be done by bringing the boss as close as possible to half HP, then applying Vulnerable and spending as much energy as possible playing Attacks.
** With Wrath, the Watcher is particularly good at killing or nearly killing Slime Boss before it can split.
* Slime Boss and its Slimes will clog your Deck with Slimed the longer the fight goes on, particularly harshly on higher ascensions.
** Evolve and Fire Breathing turn those Slimed into advantage.
* Sources of AOE damage like Whirlwind are effective against the Slimes that spawn after Slime Boss Splits.
